t.3.19.2: They saw the mighty Rāma seated in the leaf-hut together with Sītā, the princess of Videha, and with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.19.1: Then the dreadful Śūrpaṇakhā, having come to the hermitage of Rāghava, pointed out to the rākṣasas the two brothers together with Sītā.
t.3.19.3: Seeing them, and that rākṣasī who had come with them, the illustrious Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa of blazing splendour.
t.3.19.4: For a moment, O Saumitri, stay close beside Sītā; I shall slay these who have come here following her track.
t.3.19.5: Then, having heard these words of Rāma, whose self was known, Lakṣmaṇa honored Rāma's words, saying, "So be it."
t.3.19.6: Rāghava too, the righteous-souled one, strung his great bow adorned with gold, and spoke to those rākṣasas.
t.3.19.7: We two are the sons of Daśaratha, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who have entered the Daṇḍaka forest, hard to traverse, together with Sītā.
t.3.19.8: We two are self-restrained ascetics who live on fruits and roots, follow dharma, and dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest. For what reason do you seek to harm us?
t.3.19.9: At the command of the sages I have come, bow in hand, to slay you evil-natured ones, who do wrongs in the great forest.
t.3.19.10: Stay right where you are, content; you ought not to approach. If you have any use for your lives here, turn back, O night-rangers!
t.3.19.11: Having heard those words of his, those fourteen rākṣasas, slayers of brahmins, spears in hand, spoke in great fury.
t.3.19.12: Their eyes reddened with rage, the fearsome ones, exultant, turned to Rāma, whose eyes were red at the corners, whose speech was harsh and unpleasant, and whose valor they had witnessed.
t.3.19.13: Having roused the wrath of our lord Khara, the great-souled one, you yourself shall give up your life today, slain by us in battle.
t.3.19.14: What power have you, alone, even to stand before us, who are many, at the forefront of battle, let alone to fight us in combat?
t.3.19.16: Having spoken thus, those fourteen enraged Rākṣasas, with weapons and swords upraised, rushed straight at Rāma. They hurled those spears at Rāghava, who was hard to conquer.
t.3.19.15: By these iron clubs, spears and battle-axes of ours, hurled by our arms, you shall give up your life, your valour, and the bow gripped tight in your hand.
t.3.19.17: Kākutstha cut down all those fourteen spears with just as many arrows adorned with gold.
t.3.19.18: Then, after that, the greatly splendid one, utterly enraged, took up fourteen iron arrows, sun-like in brilliance and sharpened on stone.
t.3.19.19: Seizing his bow and drawing it, Rāghava took aim at the rākṣasas as his targets and released his arrows, like Śatakratu hurling his thunderbolts.
t.3.19.20: And the arrows, with golden shafts and golden ornaments, blazing in the sky, became equal in splendor to great meteors.
t.3.19.21: Those arrows, piercing with force the chests of the Rākṣasas, flew out drenched in blood, and then, roaring like thunderbolts, sank into the earth.
t.3.19.22: With their hearts pierced, their limbs drenched in blood, disfigured and lifeless, they fell to the ground like trees whose roots have been cut.
t.3.19.23: Seeing them fallen upon the ground, the rākṣasī, stupefied with rage and terrified, once again let forth a dreadful cry there.
t.3.19.24: Roaring a great roar, Śūrpaṇakhā swiftly approached Khara once more, her blood now somewhat dried, and, stricken with pain, she fell down again like a creeper oozing its sap.
t.3.19.25: But seeing the rākṣasas struck down in battle, Śūrpaṇakhā ran back again from there, and she, the sister of Khara, recounted everything, the slaughter of those rākṣasas in its entirety.
